cases.contract: Apply -I to an arbitrary input, including when controlled. XZXZ = -I exactly.
cases.limitations: This replaces R(I,2*pi) with exact gates. The test must distinguish the sign under coherent control.

cases.contract: Apply CNOT(0,2) CNOT(0,1) H(0); |000> becomes (|000>+|111>)/sqrt(2).
cases.limitations: The upstream loop is specialized to three wires. The full three-wire unitary extension is also tested.

cases.contract: Return 1 for |+> and 0 for |->. For any input rho, P(1)=(1+Tr(X rho))/2.
cases.limitations: Measurement consumes the input; no post-measurement qubit is returned. The X before Z measurement preserves the upstream Boolean polarity.

cases.contract: Consume the message and Alice half; return ((phase, parity), corrected Bob). Each branch has weight 1/4 and preserves the input density operator and any reference correlations.
cases.limitations: Upstream corrections Z then X are retained. One branch differs from X then Z by a phase, irrelevant after the classical measurement. Reset of already consumed logical owners is omitted.

cases.contract: Encode classical (phase, parity) into one Bell half, then decode exactly to the same two bits.
cases.limitations: The upstream message record becomes a CBit pair. Tests cover all four classical messages; this is not coherent transmission of quantum message registers.

cases.contract: For the fixed hidden string (1,1), H^2 diag((-1)^(a xor b)) H^2 sends |00> to |11>.
cases.limitations: The input size is two; the hidden string is fixed at (1,1). Phase kickback replaces an explicitly retained |-> answer qubit; no general oracle parameter or host decoding is claimed.

cases.contract: One Grover iteration with one marked item 11: D O H^2, D=2|++><++|-I, O=diag(1,1,1,-1). |00> maps to |11> with phase +1.
cases.limitations: Two input bits and one iteration. The upstream global-phase correction is preserved by the sign of the standard reflection.

cases.contract: Three-bit coherent QPE for U=T. On |000>|b>, the phase bits encode b/8, first bit least significant; the target survives.
cases.limitations: Initialization/measurement live in main. Returns raw bits and target instead of a floating estimate and reset. The fixed precision and eighth-root phase are explicit.

cases.contract: For a=a0+2*a1 and b=b0+2*b1, map |a,b> to |a,(a+b) mod 4> with amplitude +1 on the whole input space.
cases.limitations: Specializes unsigned equal two-bit registers. Uses a direct carry circuit instead of the general upstream decomposition; upstream T-count formulas are not transferred.

cases.contract: Map |a,b> to |a,b xor a>, for two-bit registers; phase +1.
cases.limitations: Fixed width two. QLI wire order is explicitly least significant first.

cases.contract: Map |a,b,t> to |a,b,t xor [a<b]>, where a=a0+2*a1 and b=b0+2*b1.
cases.limitations: Finite total basis permutation checked by existing enumeration; not a scalable comparator synthesis or a reproduction of the upstream gate count.

cases.contract: For address a=a0+2*a1, XOR data[a] into the two-bit target, with data=[1,2,3,0]; retain address and arbitrary target.
cases.limitations: This selected affine data table has a short CNOT/X circuit. It does not implement general unary-iteration QROM, multidimensional loading or symbolic resource estimates.

cases.contract: Compute a positive-control AND into a clean auxiliary, phase it by Z and uncompute: diag(1,1,1,-1) on the two inputs.
cases.limitations: A compute/use/uncompute adaptation of And, not its standalone signature. QLI checks exact zero return; it does not use the upstream measurement-based uncompute or inherit its T-count.

cases.contract: F4[y,x]=exp(2*pi*i*x*y/4)/2 with output reversal included. Integer bit order is first leaf least significant.
cases.limitations: Two-bit specialization of the mathematical Fourier transform using the existing QLI library. The explicit integer encoding adapter differs from upstream big-endian register presentation.

cases.contract: Two-bit coherent QPE with rectangular/uniform window and U=S=T^2. On |00>|b>, report b/4 and retain the target.
cases.limitations: Two precision bits, one target bit and exact powers; no arbitrary state preparation window, precision calculator or symbolic sizes.

cases.contract: I-2|++><++|, with prepare=H^2 and upstream global_phase=+1.
cases.limitations: This is the negative of std::routines::reflect_uniform2. Controlled interference tests retain that distinction; no arbitrary prepare oracle is accepted here.

cases.contract: Apply RY(pi/2) RX(pi/2) exactly, including scalar phase. From |0>, the Z expectation is zero.
cases.limitations: Both continuous parameters are specialized to pi/2. Host-side expectation evaluation is tested; differentiation and optimization remain outside QLI.

cases.contract: The measured teleportation instrument returns ((phase, parity), Bob), each branch weight 1/4, preserving reference correlations.
cases.limitations: Uses the demo mid-circuit measurement and conditional-correction formulation. Arbitrary state preparation is supplied by the caller; no state-vector loading or postselection.

cases.contract: One layer exp(-i*alpha*sum X) exp(-i*gamma*C) H^4 with alpha=gamma=pi/4; C=3*sum_edges(Zi*Zj+Zi+Zj)-sum_i Zi on edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,0),(2,3).
cases.limitations: Specializes the original four-node unconstrained vertex-cover graph to one layer and exact angles. No optimizer or claim of optimal vertex-cover sampling. Cost expectation is computed on the host.

cases.contract: One original gate layer: product RX(2*beta), after product exp(-i*gamma*Zi*Zj/2), after H^4. gamma=pi/2, beta=pi/4; edges (0,1),(0,3),(1,2),(2,3).
cases.limitations: Matches the demo gate convention, which omits a cost identity scalar. The scalar of every RZ/RX gate itself is retained. One fixed layer, no optimizer or shots; host computes expected cut size.

cases.contract: DoubleExcitation(pi): |0011> -> |1100>, |1100> -> -|0011>, all other basis vectors unchanged. The default input is Hartree-Fock |1100>.
cases.limitations: Finite signed-permutation specialization of the four-orbital ansatz. Host tests Z expectations and excitation signs; molecular Hamiltonian construction, continuous angles, chemistry data and VQE minimization are not imported.

cases.contract: Rot(0,pi/2,0)=RY(pi/2) on all four wires, followed by the original CNOT ring 0->1->2->3->0.
cases.limitations: One layer, fixed weights; arbitrary computational inputs tested. Training data, bias, losses, optimizer and later two-wire amplitude encoding are excluded. Host tests the Z0 expectation.

cases.contract: Three-bit QPE for PhaseShift(3*pi/4)=T^3, returning low-weight-first phase bits and the retained target.
cases.limitations: The demo angle 2*pi/5 is not exactly representable in the current coefficient domain. This explicitly changed-angle example uses 3*pi/4, not an approximation claim for the original 1/5 phase; precision is three bits.

cases.contract: The first wire is a lock meter. H, controlled FlipSign(0111), H XORs the predicate [key=0111] into that meter and preserves the four-wire key.
cases.limitations: Keeps the demo five-wire size and secret 0111. Enumerates all 32 basis inputs and probes coherent keys; no shot noise or interactive guessing game.

cases.contract: U = H^3 diag((-1)^majority(x0,x1,x2)) H^3. On |000>, outcomes 100,010,001,111 each have probability 1/4, and 000 is impossible.
cases.limitations: Specializes the balanced majority oracle on three query bits. Replaces the |- > answer register by independently checked compute/Z/uncompute phase kickback. Returns the full query register; the host identifies balanced from nonzero output. No arbitrary oracle, scalable synthesis or general Deutsch-Jozsa claim.

cases.contract: Consume both inputs and return (phase, parity), encoding the upstream integer phase + 2*parity. Branch (s,t) has effect <B_st|, where |B_st> = (|0,t> + (-1)^s |1,1 xor t>)/sqrt(2), including arbitrary reference systems.
cases.limitations: Translates the destructive Bell measurement to two CBit outputs instead of an Int. No quantum output is retained. Tests cover all four Bell labels and the complete branch/reference Choi state by nine Pauli pairs; no hardware Bell analyzer or general protocol proof.

cases.contract: For x=x0+2*x1+4*x2, map |x> to |(x+3) mod 8> with amplitude +1 on all eight basis states, including wraparound.
cases.limitations: Specializes AddK(QUInt(3), k=3) using an explicit carry circuit (+1 then +2), without temporary registers. General signed types, symbolic sizes and upstream resource-count claims are excluded.

cases.contract: For x=x0+2*x1 and y=y0+2*y1, map |x,y,t> to |x,y,t xor [x=y]> with phase +1; both target values and all input registers are preserved coherently.
cases.limitations: Specializes Equals(QUInt(2)). XOR differences, zero-controlled Toffoli and inverse XOR preserve both registers; no truth-table synthesis or upstream asymptotic cost is claimed.

cases.contract: For selector s (first wire) and data d, U=(H_s tensor I_d) SELECT(I,Z) (H_s tensor I_d), so U|s,d>=|s xor d,d>. Its zero-selector block is (I+Z)/2=|0><0|.
cases.limitations: Preserves the original equal coefficients and I/Z operators. Chooses H as an explicit unitary completion of PREP|0>=|+>; it does not identify all columns with an unspecified upstream StatePrep completion. The full QLI unitary is tested separately from the projected-block equation. Both owners are returned: selector zero return, deterministic projection, postselection, arbitrary coefficients and general LCU/QSVT are not provided.

cases.contract: Apply S(x2)^dagger S(x1), S(x)=RX(x[0]) tensor RX(x[1]), for x1=(pi,pi/2), x2=(pi/2,0). The net operator is RX(pi/2) on each wire with exact scalar phase. On |00>, probability 00 and the kernel overlap equal 1/4.
cases.limitations: Specializes default RX AngleEmbedding to two features and exact quarter-turns. The host reads the all-zero probability instead of an imported Hermitian observable. No dataset, SVM, PyTorch, optimization, gradients or continuous-angle API is included.

cases.contract: Map |a,b> to |b,a> with scalar +1 on the entire two-qubit space, preserving arbitrary reference correlations.
cases.limitations: Translates the original three-CNOT SWAP on two fixed inputs. Both owners are returned; arrays, device placement and general-size registers are excluded.

cases.contract: Map |c,a,b> to |c,a,b> for c=0 and |c,b,a> for c=1, with scalar +1 on all eight basis inputs.
cases.limitations: Translates Controlled SWAP to coherent qif and an ordinary three-CNOT helper. The control and both targets survive; no classical measurement of the control or general array API is introduced.

cases.contract: For x=x0+2*x1, map |x> to |x xor 1> with scalar +1 on all four basis inputs; only the low bit changes.
cases.limitations: Specializes XorK(QUInt(2), k=1). First-leaf-low ordering explicitly adapts the upstream register encoding. Signed types, symbolic constants/sizes and imported resource-count claims are excluded.

cases.contract: For x=x0+2*x1, map |x> to |3-x> = |x xor 3> with scalar +1 on all four basis inputs.
cases.limitations: Specializes BitwiseNot(QUInt(2)), flipping both bits and returning the same owner shape. General signed/modular types, symbolic sizes and resource estimation are excluded.

cases.contract: Apply RX(pi/2)=(I-iX)/sqrt(2), including the exact scalar phase. On |0>, Z measurement is uniform and <Z>=0.
cases.limitations: Specializes params=(pi/2,0), so the original RY is identity. Z expectation is aggregated on the host from the returned distribution. Reuses the known exact rotation decomposition; no optimizer, gradients, continuous angles or upstream framework execution.

cases.contract: For meter m (first leaf) and one-bit key k, H_m controlled(Z_k) H_m maps |m,k> to |m xor k,k> with scalar +1, retaining both owners and all coherent inputs.
cases.limitations: Narrows the original four-bit secret 0111 to one-bit secret 1 with num_wires=2. Preserves the H/controlled-FlipSign/H mechanism. Basis preparation and readout live in main; returns both owners instead of one sampled bit. No shot-noise, interactive guessing game or claim to port the original five-wire configuration.

cases.contract: Apply H to the first two wires, XOR them into the third, then flip the third: |000> becomes the uniform odd-parity state. The complete unitary extension retains signed input columns.
cases.limitations: Specializes the recursive source to three wires and parity 1. The common even/odd recursive bodies share their Hadamards; their conditional last-wire X is a CNOT. This is deterministic preparation, not the postselection alternative.

cases.contract: The index-3 Bell preparation X(second) Z(second) CNOT(first,second) H(first) sends |00> to (|01>-|10>)/sqrt(2) in upstream first/second-wire notation, retaining its sign on every input.
cases.limitations: Specializes index to 3 and two wires. It returns the complete unitary extension, not a general classical-index API or a Bell measurement.

cases.contract: For x=x0+2*x1, map |x,t> to |x,t xor [x<3]> with scalar +1, retaining arbitrary target values and input correlations.
cases.limitations: Specializes unsigned width to 2 and threshold to 3. Uses X(target) followed by Toffoli, since [x<3]=not(x0 and x1); no general comparator synthesis or upstream resource bound is transferred.

cases.contract: For x=x0+2*x1, map |x,t> to |x,t xor [x=1]> with scalar +1 and restore both input bits.
cases.limitations: Specializes unsigned width to 2 and constant to 1. The mixed-polarity controls explicitly invert and restore the high bit; no symbolic-size equality API or imported gate-count claim.

cases.contract: Apply RY(pi/2)=(I-iY)/sqrt(2)=[[1,-1],[1,1]]/sqrt(2) exactly, including the second-column sign.
cases.limitations: Specializes params=(0,pi/2), making RX identity. The exact H Z implementation introduces no global scalar. No optimizer, continuous angle API, gradient or upstream framework execution.

cases.contract: Apply exp(-i*pi*Z0*Z1/4): equal bits receive exp(-i*pi/4), unequal bits exp(+i*pi/4). Retain both owners and the absolute scalar phase.
cases.limitations: Extracts one edge from U_C at gamma=pi/2. This is the cost-layer factor CNOT/RZ/CNOT, not the full four-node graph, mixer or optimizer. The two-wire specialization preserves the upstream rotation sign.
